_comment: Photographs for the p3 chapters (p3c01-p3c24), fetched and processed 2026-08-22. Every licence below was re-read off the file's own description page - Commons extmetadata for Commons files, the live Flickr page for the Flickr file, and the distribution's own license.terms for the Tcl/Tk file - never off an article that used the image. Twelve files for nine subjects' worth of chapters: p3c15 and p3c17 name two people each and get one file per person, and p3c08 is a single uncropped group photograph containing both named subjects. Photographs are downscaled to 480px on the long edge with EXIF stripped and saved JPEG quality 82 progressive; nothing is cropped. The 'reaudit' object records the second look at all fifteen class-B subjects in this range so the next pass need not repeat it: fourteen confirmed, one overturned (p3c12 Graham Cormode).

p3c01.subject: F. G. (Gordon) Foster
p3c01.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Wikidata (P18) incl. namesake disambiguation; Wikipedia lead image and image list in en/de/fr/ja/ko/zh/it/es/nl/da/ru; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons and others, licence filter cc0/by/by-sa/pdm); Wikidata Q15441894 'Irish mathematician' exists but carries no P18; en-wiki article 'Gordon Foster' exists and has no lead image and no portrait in its image list
p3c01.conclusion: Confirmed. He is now identifiable on Wikidata and en-wiki, but no free photograph is attached to either and none surfaced on Commons, Openverse or any CC-filtered aggregate. Trinity College Dublin and obituary photographs remain all rights reserved.
p3c01.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p3c02.subject: Dale Grover, Martin King and Cliff Kushler
p3c02.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Wikidata (P18) incl. namesake disambiguation; Wikipedia lead image and image list in en/de/fr/ja/ko/zh/it/es/nl/da/ru; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons and others, licence filter cc0/by/by-sa/pdm); Openverse turned up two Flickr frames by JD Lasica from TechCrunch50 2008 titled 'Swype CEO', described 'Swype's CEO, Cliff Kushler' and one tagged 'cliffkushler'
p3c02.conclusion: Confirmed, but only just, and this is the near miss worth recording. Openverse indexes those two frames as CC BY 2.0, and the identification is sound - the photographer names Kushler in the description. The live Flickr pages, however, now report license id 0, 'All rights reserved', with the licence link pointing at Flickr's 'Using Flickr images shared by other members' help page rather than a Creative Commons deed. The photographer has re-licensed since Openverse ingested them, so the CC record is stale and the photographs are NOT free. Rejected on licence, not on identity. Nothing at all for Dale Grover or Martin King.
p3c02.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p3c12.subject: Graham Cormode and S. Muthukrishnan
p3c12.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Wikidata (P18) incl. namesake disambiguation; Wikipedia lead image and image list in en/de/fr/ja/ko/zh/it/es/nl/da/ru; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons and others, licence filter cc0/by/by-sa/pdm); Openverse surfaced a Flickr frame titled 'Graham Cormode' by user robennals, tagged sigmod/beijing/china/conference; licence re-read off the live Flickr page (license id 4, 'Some rights reserved', deed URL creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/); identity corroborated against Wikidata Q59696755 (British computer scientist, born 1977) and the photographer's own description
p3c12.conclusion: OVERTURNED for Cormode. A free photograph does exist: Robert Ennals photographed him at SIGMOD 2007 in Beijing and published it CC BY 2.0. Field, era and venue all match - SIGMOD 2007 was held in Beijing in June 2007, the photograph was posted 25 June 2007, and Cormode was then at AT&T Labs-Research working on exactly the streaming and sketching topics SIGMOD covers. The photographer's note, 'I hadn't seen Graham for ten years', places them as contemporaries from about 1997, when Cormode (b. 1977) was an undergraduate. Fetched as photo/p3c12-cormode.jpg. It is a candid in a crowded room rather than a portrait, so the CSS crop matters. S. Muthukrishnan is CONFIRMED class B - Wikidata Q102165467 has no P18, the only Commons hits for the surname are unrelated people, and nothing free is indexed.

p3c21.subject: Drew Major
p3c21.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Wikidata (P18) incl. namesake disambiguation; Wikipedia lead image and image list in en/de/fr/ja/ko/zh/it/es/nl/da/ru; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons and others, licence filter cc0/by/by-sa/pdm); re-read File:2005 dmajor bw.jpg off its own Commons description page and raw wikitext (it is the P18 on Wikidata Q16187186 and the lead image on the en-wiki article, so it looks authoritative at a glance)
p3c21.conclusion: Confirmed, and the original reasoning holds exactly. The raw wikitext is {{PD-author|Drew Major Press Photo Released into PD to the Utah Technology Council and online sites}} with Author and Source both filled in as the non-person string 'Utah Technology Council Public Domain'. {{PD-author}} requires the actual copyright holder - the photographer - to make the release; here an uploader asserts that an unnamed photographer's press photo was released to a third-party trade body. No photographer named, no VRT ticket. This is the press-kit pattern the brief flags and it does not survive scrutiny.
p3c21.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p3c22.subject: Koichiro Miyahara

p3c22.conclusion: Confirmed, and the namesake trap is real and now documented on Wikidata. The single Commons file of that name is the novelist, not the exchange president. Reuters and Kyodo hold the 2020 press-conference frames.
p3c22.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found
